questions.prompt: Why simulate a plan symbolically on the newly observed scene before executing it?
options: It finds the first step whose preconditions fail without moving the robot.
It guarantees that the plan will succeed physically on the real robot.
It removes the need for perception, since the symbolic state is exact.
It makes the plan shorter by merging redundant steps automatically.
questions.explanation: Symbolic validation is cheap and detects precondition violations early, but cannot guarantee physical success.

questions.prompt: A plan reads 6 externally perceived facts, each correct with probability 0.95 independently. Probability that all are correct? (3 decimals)
What per-fact confidence is needed so that 5 independent facts are all correct with probability 0.85? (3 decimals)
In plan a1..a4, a1 adds clear(A) and a3 needs clear(A). What is this relation called, and what threatens it?
options: A goal condition; a1 threatens it by adding clear(A) twice.
A causal link; a2 would threaten it if a2 deletes clear(A).
A precondition of a1; a3 threatens it by needing clear(A).
A conflict link; a4 would threaten it by deleting clear(A) after a3.
questions.explanation: A causal link is producer-fact-consumer; a step between them that deletes the fact is a threat.

questions.prompt: Logs show an object is lifted 95% of the time when 'gripper closed' is on, but a person also lifts objects by hand. Which statement is right?
options: Nothing can be learned from logs at all, so only new experiments are of any use.
The effect of closing the gripper on lifting is 0.95, as read directly from the logs.
The lift causes the gripper to close, so the causal arrow points the other way here.
The conditional frequency is not the effect of commanding the gripper; use an intervention.
questions.explanation: Conditioning on the signal mixes the robot's effect with other causes; intervention isolates the effect.

questions.prompt: A blind replay executes a 7-step plan whose first invalid step has index 4 (0-based) in the changed scene. How many steps are physically executed before the failure is hit?
Predicted state after step 2 contains ontable(C) but the camera reports on(C,B). Describe what the robot should do and what information it uses.
rubric: Computes the difference between predicted and observed facts (missing ontable(C), extra on(C,B)).
Updates the symbolic state to the observation and replans from it.
Names a way to check the cause (re-detect, re-grasp) and avoid repeating the failure.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
